text: Kingsmoor FC scores first with Viktor Quinlan’s penalty from the penalty spot, about 10 metres out on the left side of Westport Albion’s goal at the north end, setting the score 1-0 early in the 8th minute [#152]. Just four minutes later, Quinlan strikes again, finishing from the center inside the 9-metre box after a patient build-up passing across the midfield and flanks [#222]. Westport Albion responds with quick, direct attacks: Rafael Delacroix scores twice within eight minutes, first from close to the right side near Kingsmoor’s goal, then after a cross from the left flank, leveling the match at 2-2 by the 30th minute [#401] [#553]. In the second half, Kenji Rahman gives Westport the lead with a goal following a cross from the right side around 5 metres from goal [#983]. Kingsmoor faces a setback with a red card at the 81st minute. Still, they quickly respond with an equalizer from Luca Iversen, arriving at the near post on the left side inside the box and scoring from a cross, making it 3-3 [#1516]. Both teams show tactical shifts during the match, with Kingsmoor pressing higher in the second half, while Westport aims to protect their lead by dropping deeper late on [#1187] [#1459].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for audio audience in en

- Viktor Quinlan scored twice early for Kingsmoor FC including a penalty at 8' with xG 0.76 and an open play goal at 12' with xG 0.291, setting Kingsmoor 2-0 up [#152, #222].
- Rafael Delacroix scored twice for Westport Albion at 22' (xG 0.816) and 30' (xG 0.976) to level the match 2-2 [#401, #553].
- Kenji Rahman put Westport Albion ahead 3-2 at 51' with a goal from open play having xG 0.705 [#983].
- Felix Barros of Kingsmoor FC got a second yellow card red card around 81', putting Kingsmoor a man down [#1495].
- Luca Iversen equalized for Kingsmoor FC at 82' with an xG of 0.888 assisted by Mason Morales to make it 3-3 [#1516].

- Kingsmoor FC opened the scoring with a penalty by Viktor Quinlan at 8 minutes, indicating early pressure or a defensive error by Westport Albion leading to a spot kick rather than open play build-up [152].
- Kingsmoor’s second goal at 12 minutes arose from a sustained build-up over 26 seconds with 8 passes starting from a regain, demonstrating their 4-4-2 formation’s capacity for patient, wide, crossing play involving multiple players and ball circulation before a medium assist from Felix Duarte to Quinlan finished off a move reflecting composure and structure in their attack [222].
- Westport Albion responded both goals through quick regains and direct, vertical passing patterns in their 4-4-2 structure: first at 22 minutes with 7 passes over 25 seconds culminating in a short assist to Rafael Delacroix who scored close-range, showing their ability to exploit regained possession efficiently and attack swiftly [401]; and again at 30 minutes via a 10-pass build-up over nearly 40 seconds that included a cross from Dylan Rahman leading to Delacroix’s close-range finish, emphasizing their vertical, direct style with crosses delivering goal chances [553].
- Kingsmoor applied a significant pressing trap early in the second half, reflected in a decrease in Westport’s attacking threat and increased turnovers (e.g., Kingsmoor's 13 high turnovers and improved pressing stats after tactical changes at 65’), attempting to chase the game by pressing higher, playing more direct, and pushing their line higher - this tactical shift was pivoted around regains and quicker attacks, but still allowed Westport chances given their continued vertical passing threat [1187].
- Late in the match, Westport Albion altered their approach to protect the lead by dropping deeper and slowing the tempo, reducing pressing intensity and field tilt, which appeared aimed at maintaining defensive solidity and controlling possession, as suggested by the drop in their box touches and shots after the 79th-minute tactical change [1459].
- Despite being a man down after Felix Barros’s red card at 81 minutes, Kingsmoor FC capitalized quickly from a regain and wide crossing play leading to an equaliser by Luca Iversen at 82 minutes, highlighting their resilience and exploitation of wide areas to deliver crosses for high-probability chances characteristic of their 4-4-2 wide style [1516].
